The integration of formal verification and testing techniques aims to provide cost-effective security for critical systems, but blending these methods has proven challenging. Our geometric approach bridges this gap, leveraging compilation as a foundation to generate test cases that target specific underproven areas of a program, illustrated with a syntax tree diagram.

We provide a simplified proof of the connection between Clear Serre weights and a specific Kummer theory introduced by Breuil. Our argument shows that a specific field extension used by Breuil to define certain representations of GL_2 via Kummer theory actually reduces to a well-known Mumford-Serre extension when applied to GL_2. Consequently, we can use this simpler version of the extension to define representations of GL_2 via Kummer theory in place of the more complex one.

Advanced composite materials that incorporate nanofillers into polymer matrices have a potential capability to sense damage in real-time, thereby improving safety in working environments.  
The principle of this functionality relies on changes in electrical conductivity that occur when a material is damaged.  
However, measurable shifts in resistance are often difficult to quantify in macroscopic scales without causing additional damage.  
To address this issue, a genetic algorithm was integrated with electrical impedance tomography to precisely visualize and measure damage patterns within vinyl ester resin composites that contain carbon nanotubes.  
The result of this study demonstrates the ability to shape damage patterns based on desired electrical signals, thereby enabling monitored materials to detect and distinguish between new damage and existing patterns.  
This breakthrough has the potential to enhance safety in extreme working environments where regular inspection methods may be unreliable or impossible to carry out.

Our work introduces a tensor formalism for Euclidean spaces centered on geometric tensor operators representing point, direction, and rotation. This novel approach streamlines the traditional Euclidean tensor theory by incorporating basic geometric concepts early on, even at the vectorization stage of the Euclidean space. As a result, essential Euclidean properties emerge more naturally when generalizing the description to a curved Riemannian manifold. This approach is particularly beneficial for those seeking a rigorous mathematical foundation for the intrinsic physical principles underlying general relativity.

If a right-angled Artin graph experiences a splitting into two components through an edge cycle of length at least 4, we prove that this graph can be reconfigured into a product structure where the components correspond to subgroups. This revelation establishes that higher-dimensional products of Euclidean spaces are fundamental to the origin of subgroups with positive fundamental groups within right-angled Coxeter groups, contrasting with the behavior of right-angled Coxeter groups in dimension one.

The advent of graphical processing units (GPUs) has created a demand for efficient matrix inversion algorithms that can be parallelized effectively. While the Neumann series method has been previously proposed to compute the inverse of a non-singular matrix, we introduce a new iteration method that improves convergence speed by utilizing the concept of Pad approximants. Our innovative approach consists of a novel iteration formula, a sophisticated parameter update strategy, and an optimized storage format specifically designed for GPU acceleration. Comparisons with existing methods, including Neumann series, demonstrate that our Pad approximant-based technique offers significant generalization possibilities and superior performance.

Contextual linear bandits is an efficient framework applicable to various real-world decision-making scenarios such as personalized recommendations and resource allocation. A significant limitation of existing studies lies in their confinement to simple settings where features are binary or from a finite set. This paper addresses the learning problems in contextual linear bandits within a distributed setting, focusing on a more practical and prevalent scenario where the context vectors are infinite-dimensional. In this distributed context, the context vectors are local to agents, and the goal is to minimize the regret relative to a known set of valid decision-making strategies. Since the context features are not directly observable by the coordinator, both the coordinator and the learning agent must infer the context vectors and make optimal decisions based on limited information exchange. This paper proposes a novel learning protocol enabling the learning agent and the coordinator to collaborate effectively without sharing the context setting. This protocol achieves a regret bound polynomial in the dimension of the feature space and the number of context segments, comparable to contexts from a finite set. The proof of this result leverages a new technique for context approximation, which employs a combination of local information and the learned strategy to estimate the context vector.

A phenomenon called vertical shear instability (VSI) occurs in protoplanetary disks and is influenced by electric dust particles. To understand how the VSI works in these disks, a theoretical model was created that takes into account the structure of the disk and the forces acting upon it. This model considers gravity, pressure, and shear forces as well as the evolution of dust particles. As the dust particles settle towards the bottom of the disk, the VSI tends to disappear in the mid-layers of the disk due to reduced instability growth rates. This is because dust settlement changes the way forces interact with each other. Additionally, since radiation is trapped more effectively in clear upper regions of the disk, a stronger temperature gradient develops, which can lead to another type of instability called gravity shear instability (GSI). This is more likely to occur in the outer regions of the disk as it grows at a faster rate compared to the VSI.

This research focuses on harmonic functions within the context of a particular type of manifold where the Ricci curvature decreases over time. We have proven that bounded harmonic functions are constant in specific situations where the dimension of the manifold is at most 4 or when the manifold's curvature characteristics meet certain conditions. This accomplishment extends upon earlier findings. Additionally, our result implies that a certain type of theorem established by Li and Yau does not hold in all cases when the dimension of the manifold is 5 or greater, specifically under the conditions where the scalar curvature remains consistent across the manifold and the manifold experiences a transition from expanded to shrunk states over time.

A subtle modification in a neural network called a backdoor triggers malicious behavior when a specific trigger pattern is present. Researchers have commonly used weight normalization techniques to craft these modifications, but this process is static and often leads to performance issues. We introduce a dynamic backdoor concept where the modification changes with the neural network and relies on a previously trained poisoned model. This new approach allows for more efficient crafting of backdoors, reducing the need for retraining the entire model and utilizing global average pooling to detect the changes. Our experiments on various deep learning architectures demonstrate that this method is highly effective and often undetectable, especially in longer image sequences. Furthermore, we find that the poisoning rate is significantly lower when using global mean pooling to craft the changes.

In the context of a distributed machine learning framework designed to respect privacy, a crucial challenge lies in ensuring consistency among models across a network of devices with limited computation capabilities and communication bandwidth. A significant source of difficulty in this process is a phenomenon where a device's local data becomes outdated as a result of a global model's update bypassing that specific device during a given round of learning. To address this problem, a novel random walk strategy has been proposed, enabling a global model to traverse and update heterogeneous data sets in a manner that adapts to each device's individual characteristics without requiring a significant increase in computation or communication overhead. This approach utilizes a random walk mechanism to replicate global models across neighboring devices, building upon a variance-reduced gradient method, and incorporates a parameter update rule designed to accelerate convergence. Theoretical analysis confirms that the proposed method converges to an optimal global model, and extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in various data distribution scenarios, outperform existing techniques.

A novel, simplicity-oriented consistency regularization semi-supervised learning strategy has been presented to enhance medical image segmentation in under-trained models. This method focuses on enforcing data reconciliation on boundary regions of preliminary segmentations without the need for additional deep learning-based consistency regularization training steps. Additionally, an optimal training data selection strategy has been introduced to maximize the efficiency of the consistency regularization training process. The proposed approach demonstrates its superiority over existing methods through evaluations on four publicly available medical image datasets, including one private dataset. The results indicate that this data-driven selection and simplicity-oriented consistency regularization strategy yields excellent performance with reduced computational costs compared to other consistency regularization training methods.

In 1881, the Sagnac effect was discovered, later explained by quantum mechanics in 1935 through the Einstein-Podolsk-Rosen paradox. Although initially seen as analogous to nonlocal correlations in multi-particle systems, the Sagnac effect's significance in establishing nonlocality for single-particles has been overlooked. Using the language of entanglement and nonlocality, we reinterpret the Sagnac effect and a similar phenomenon observed in interference patterns as instances of nonlocal correlations between a particle's path and its internal state. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these nonlocal interpretations remain valid even after the which-path information is partially lost, providing a new perspective on the persistence of nonlocality in the face of decoherence.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence within Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) has significantly improved traffic management and safety, but data privacy issues and security concerns have become increasingly pressing issues. Both Federated Learning and Blockchain technologies offer promising solutions to these problems, but their effective combination requires further exploration and understanding. This paper conducts an in-depth review and analysis of Blockchain-Federated Learning (BFL) systems designed for IoVs, exploring their architectures, key issues, and potential directions for future research. BFL systems can be categorized into various types based on their design principles, including probabilistic, contract-based, and identity management schemes, among others. Furthermore, BFL systems can be evaluated based on their performance in terms of privacy protection, security guarantees, and efficiency. This research provides a comprehensive summary of BFL systems' design principles and implementations, laying the foundation for the development of more advanced and effective solutions that better meet the demanding needs of IoVs environments. This work is particularly beneficial for academic researchers, industry professionals, and policy makers in the fields of vehicular communications, machine learning, and Blockchain technology.

Deep learning models such as LSTMs have been widely used for video recognition due to their ability to handle long-term dependencies. Despite the successful results, the high computational costs of these models have limited their deployment on resource-constrained devices. In an attempt to overcome this obstacle, both hardware and software designs can be optimized to enhance the efficiency of LSTM networks. However, existing studies have often focused solely on hardware or software designs, failing to fully exploit the potential improvements that combining the two can bring. This paper proposes an integrated hardware and software design that significantly improves the efficiency of LSTM networks through tensor decomposition and hardware optimization techniques. By sharing memory resources and computing units across recurrent layers and rows, as well as eliminating redundant operations, the proposed design achieves substantial speedups in terms of area, energy, and latency. The proposed architecture also outperforms state-of-the-art models such as GRUs and BILSTMs while maintaining similar recognition accuracy.

We provide novel examples of composite rings where the concept of prime elements and irreducible elements aligns perfectly. Specifically, in the ring R = k[x_1,...,x_n]/<x_1^2+x_2^2,...,x_n^2+x_{n+1}^2>, with k being the field of complex numbers, we demonstrate that unital complex structures on the free algebra of polynomials of degree one in n variables preserve the equivalence of prime and irreducible elements. Additionally, we present new iterative methods for the composition of polynomials over the field of rational numbers of degree at least two that achieve the same goal. Notably, in the field of rational numbers of degree three, we establish iterative formulas of the composition of two specific linear complex structures on the free algebra of polynomials of degree one in 2 variables that maintain the consistent notion of prime elements.

Our study addresses the Schrödinger equation enhanced by a focusing nonlinear term, considered in a exterior domain under the influence of a convex obstacle. A nonlinearity of mass-critical type is under examination. First, we establish that solutions within the ball of critical radius are unstable. Subsequently, we identify an infinite sequence of initial conditions, growing unbounded in norm, that give rise to explosive behavior. Moreover, we confirm the global stability of vacuum solution when considering initial data within the ball of maximally allowable radius. It is important to note that our findings extend previous results obtained in unconstrained spaces.

We provide a novel proof that local characteristic-subfield reductions of a variety defined over the integers are equivalent to local extensions of the variety's defining parametric polynomial. Specifically, given a variety $V$ in an $n$-dimensional space over a algebra $\mathbb{k}[t_1,...,t_r]$, and its image $V'$ in an $n$-dimensional space over the field of fractions of the algebra, if the rank of the variety at a generic point is $n$, then the local defining equations of the variety at a general point in the algebra can be derived from the local defining equations of the image of the variety at a general point in the field of fractions, within the power series ring of a field.

Hypothesis evaluation employs a variety of approaches, each with its own strengths and weaknesses, and the choice between them often depends on the specific context. In contrast, Bayesian model comparison utilizes Bayes factors to directly compare rival models, effectively blending evidence and initial assumptions. Despite their apparent simplicity, Bayes factor calculations can be deceivingly complex, as they implicitly incorporate certain aspects of statistical testing that are often overlooked. This paper delves into the underlying issues causing Bayes factor discrepancies and proposes a framework for navigating these challenges, incorporating practical advice and illustrative examples drawn from both theoretical and real-world scenarios, including the R package BayesFactor.

Discourse markers are words that facilitate the connection between sentences, presenting a significant challenge for automatic semantic evaluation. To tackle this issue, we introduce our discourse semantic model, built upon BERT-base-UNC, and trained on the sample set of discourse annotated corpus, specifically tailored to assess the semantic equivalence of discourse markers. Our 10-layered model outperforms approaches that utilize discourse-free sentence pairs, and we find that at least four layers are necessary for effective discourse semantic evaluation. Furthermore, we identify the distinctive role that discourse markers play in analyzing sentence relationships and propose a novel classification system based on those relationships.

Recently, a generalization of the twist operator within the Jordanian quantization framework was introduced. This one-parameter extension of the original twist operator is instrumental in creating invariant bifunctionals for the $sl_2$ loop algebra, which is a modified version of the $sl_2$ Lie algebra with an additional central element. The (doubled) $sl_2$ loop algebra is a specific type of Hopf algebra that can be further generalized into a family of Hopf algebras. This family includes the Jordanian quantization as a special case, where the twist operator plays a key role in defining a splitting of the coproduct. The resulting invariant bifunctionals are significant in a variety of mathematical fields, particularly in the study of integrable systems and symmetry groups.

This research has been inspired by the concept of regular expressions and aims to develop an algorithm for analyzing and resolving the pattern defined in these expressions when they extend beyond the basic definition. According to the revised pattern, special operators such as complement, intersection, and subtraction are incorporated into the regular expression syntax. The objective is to determine whether the pattern represented by these expressions corresponds to an empty set of strings and, if not, to simplify the pattern into the standard definition of regular expressions. The algorithm is grounded in the Brzozowski's derivative approach and builds upon the Wrecker's methodology while utilizing Glushkov's automaton construction and a specific canonical form for deterministic finite automata. The algorithm's efficiency is enhanced by employing Brzozowski's complementation technique and a refined sorting strategy, and its effectiveness is verified through the discovery that the revised definition still adheres to the Shannons regular expression axioms, with the exception of the intersection operator. The proposed algorithm's performance is showcased through both theoretical analysis and practical experiments.

Building upon previous work by \cite{Ferrara:1971vh}, we develop a comprehensive expression for the conformal block in flat space within both radial and spherical coordinate systems. Subsequently, we derive the OPE block in AdS space by applying the holographic dictionary as outlined in \cite{Ferrara:1971vh}. Furthermore, we obtain the Ferrara-Luk bulk operator by inverting the Ferrara-Luk boundary dictionary, and in turn, we recover the OPE block as a result of the Ferrara-Luk boundary equation. These derivations validate the consistency of this procedure. It's important to note that a more in-depth analysis is required to establish the equivalence of the Ferrera-Luk operator in Ferrara-Sanjhadyi space with the AdS holographic dictionary, which is beyond the scope of this research.

To expand the wide-field monitoring capabilities of lobster-eye optics, a novel concept called multiplexing has been introduced. In this setup, several lobster-eye optics systems are integrated into a single telescope by positioning their ring segments alternately at the outer and inner perimeters of a circular framework. This configuration results in multiple wide-field views being captured simultaneously from various angles. To determine the source of detected photons, an algorithm based on maximum-likelihood estimation and a search strategy called hierarchical grid has been developed. This method utilizes the structural information of the lobster-eye optics system to efficiently identify the source direction with a 4-fold lobster-eye optics system demonstrating a resolution of 10 degrees. A benefit of lobster-eye optics system is its scalable resolution, which can be enhanced by increasing the number of folds without compromising the field of view. This feature makes it an ideal candidate for the next generation of transient event monitors, potentially facilitating its use around extending observatories like Xenon and IceCube.

In the study of cosmology, understanding the distribution of dark matter has been enhanced by the concept of the cosmic speed field (SF). To determine the DM halo formation characteristics, we have utilized the MatterPowerPy library and focused on the halo mass function across a wide range of scales ($10^{-3}M_{\sun}$ to $10^{3}M_{\sun}$) and times ($z=0$ to $z=20$). By employing machine learning techniques, particularly random forest, we have trained a model using MatterPowerPy and analyzed the contribution of the SF on halo formation. Additionally, we have conducted a decomposition of the histogram of the halo mass function into Gaussian components and determined the best-fitting parameters for the combined distribution. Our results have shown that the SF's impact is more significant near the turnover scale, with its influence becoming less noticeable beyond $10^{3}M_{\sun}$. Overall, our findings have provided a deeper understanding of the halo mass function's origins and the SF's significance on halo formation.

One of the key challenges in metrology lies in accurately measuring weak local magnetic field gradients. A promising solution involves using atomic interferometry, but enhancing its sensitivity to these gradients is notoriously difficult. A possible remedy superconducting materials provide through their Meissner effect, which shields external magnetic fields. We propose an atomic sensor that leverages this effect to detect local magnetic field gradients. Our design employs a ring-shaped superconducting trap for atoms, which creates a linear magnetic field gradient inside the ring due to Meissner shielding of the Earth's magnetic field. A Raman radio-frequency pulse applied to atoms in the ring's superconducting trap creates an interference pattern sensitive to the internal magnetic field gradient. Our theoretical analysis predicts a sensitivity of 0.1 nT/cm for a 1-second interrogation time, with the limit constrained by the signal-to-noise ratio of atomic population measurements. Notably, we demonstrate that superconducting materials can amplify atomic sensors' sensitivity to local magnetic field gradients due to their shielding effect. This concept paves the way for precise measurements of local magnetic field gradients, which is crucial for fundamental physics research, including dark matter and proton spin crisis studies, as well as geophysics and resource exploration.

A comprehensive theoretical framework has been developed to predict the spectral characteristics of magnetic impurities located at the surface of a superconducting material. This material-specific model focuses on unpaired electrons and can be applied to both individual atoms and small clusters of materials. It incorporates a detailed description of the superconducting gap symmetry and is based on the Yu--Shiba--Rusinov state theory, extending it to include the orbital character of states and the non-point-like nature of impurities. This framework utilizes the Anisyutin--Kadomtsev extension of the theory, which considers the full shape of the impurity. It is applied to a specific case of an Mn atom and small clusters on the Nb(110) surface, providing a theoretical description of their spectral characteristics in terms of the Green's function of the superconducting material. This detailed prediction takes into consideration the spin and orbital characteristics of states and can be visually compared to experimental data obtained through various spectroscopic techniques, including SC-TMRS, TMIS, and STM. It was found that the non-point-like nature of the impurities plays a crucial role in determining the spectral characteristics of the materials. This report details our methods that led to 3rd and 10th place rankings in error rates at the ISIC 2016 and 2017 challenges, respectively. The core innovation involves using entropy to identify and discard anomalous images, enhancing the effectiveness of consensus voting when multiple deep learning models work together. Additionally, we explored the performance of one-million images collected dermoscopically, as well as various imaging techniques employed in clinical settings, including photographic images from motivated patients and visually confirmed lesions.

Due to the unique characteristics of high-luminosity muon colliders, especially their forward angle suppression of vector boson emission, we develop and discuss an enhanced version of the parton model suitable for this specific collider environment, here we call the LEHVEA, extending the conventional Vector Boson Approximation (VBA). In LEHHEIA, we precisely update VBA calculations by considering the genuine polarizations of leptons, and we present efficient algorithms for implementing these calculations at high-energy scales, including rapidity-space convolution techniques and the use of pre-computed functions to optimize computations. The LEHVEA is found to provide a good approximation of VBA results while significantly reducing computation time, making it highly suitable for Monte Carlo simulation generators, and it can still accurately describe the behavior of all particles produced during the collision, even at higher energies, here we find it provides a good fit to VBA outcomes up to 10 TeV. The LEHVEA is also discovered to be highly sensitive to new physics beyond the Standard Model, and we use it to propose new searches for heavy vector-like fermions and $Z_2$-odd scalar particles that are hidden, setting minimum detection thresholds of 4.2 TeV and 5.8 TeV, respectively, during the initial run of a future muon collider.

This paper presents proofs of Godel's first incompleteness theorem and a related diagonalization result by Rosser, along with accompanying code in Isabelle/HOL. The first proof of the theorem by Godel is reconstructed in its full detail in section 10, while an alternative version from Rosser is outlined in section 9. The diagonalization technique is explained through the Cantor-Schroder-Bernard theorem in section 8.

This article examines the instability of invariant manifold concepts in fractional-order dynamical systems when modeled in the state space. We introduce fresh interpretations of existing invariant manifold definitions, specifically for both general and linear fractional-order systems. We argue that traditional definitions stemming from analytical solutions are unsuitable for fractional-order dynamical systems exhibiting nonlinear behavior. Furthermore, we propose an alternative set of invariant manifold definitions tailored to such nonlinear systems.

This investigation explores a structural acoustic interaction inverse problem where a sensor's location needs to be determined using minimal data. A neural network is trained to predict the optimal sensor placement by analyzing the measured eigenfrequency of a structure, an task that proves theoretically challenging as the eigenfrequency values remain consistent regardless of sensor position. Despite this difficulty, our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately identify a structure's resonant modes and pinpoint the best sensor location for precise measurement, validating its effectiveness through numerical simulations and experimental validation.

In the simplest variation of the scoto-seesaw model, a minimal alteration to the Standard Model enables a tiny neutrino majorana mass through the involvement of dark sector particles, while simultaneously explaining the observed mixing of X-doubled Higgs bosons within a viable parameter range. Notably, this model can explain a potential $125$ GeV Higgs boson without requiring a new dark sector particle that mediates neutrino oscillations, as opposed to the typical mediation of the type-I seesaw mechanism. Instead, a dark sector particle that is an SU(2) singlet and mediates the $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly through an loop, while also generating the neutrino majorana mass through tree-level interaction with the Higgs boson, plays a crucial role in this process. However, this specific configuration presents a challenge due to the instability of the vacuum in the Higgs field, which can be resolved by the presence of a dark sector particle that is an SU(2) triplet and contributes to the $(g-2)_\mu$ through an oscillating loop, as well as enhancing the neutrino seesaw mechanism through an additional scale. Additionally, this model predicts a measurable decay of the dark sector particle mediating the $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly through loop-induced interactions with the Higgs boson, which can be detected in future experiments.
